function: End-to-end prediction of RSU transmit and vehicle receive beamformers directly from reflected ISAC echo signals, maximizing the downlink sum rate (p. 6, p. 8).
system: 30 GHz mmWave V2I: RSU with 256-antenna transmit UPA and 256-antenna receive UPA, full-duplex ISAC; 4 vehicles with 8x8 UPAs, LoS (p. 3, p. 10).
method: DNN with CNN, LSTM and attention (OSPB at RSU); TSPB adds a two-layer FC net per vehicle; unsupervised training on sum-rate loss with Adam (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Own simulated LoS channel (path loss exponent 3.6) with moving vehicles; 5,000 samples, 4,000 training and 1,000 testing; multipath variant in Fig. 15 (p. 10, p. 14).
test_conditions: Same simulated setting for training and testing (4,000/1,000 samples); one model trained on K=2 to 8, tested on held-out samples of those K (p. 10, p. 13).
baselines: Non-learned: MMSE, ZF, SVD beamforming with perfect CSI, EKF. Learned: E-HCL (extended HCL-Net), FC network, CNN (p. 3, p. 11).
metrics: Achievable sum-rate versus power, antennas, vehicles, height, noise, clutter, quantization bits; online runtime; training convergence (p. 11-16).
complexity: Big-O orders for training and online inference of both schemes (Eqs. 26-27, 32-34); online runtime 1.18 ms (OSPB) versus 25 ms (EKF), N=64 (p. 8, p. 10, p. 16).
q1_support: p. 3: "communicates with the vehicles through line-of-sight (LoS) links" and p. 10: "The path loss exponent" is set to 3.6, so the channel is an own simulator; p. 14: multipath uses "a spatial channel model [6]" with Laplacian angles. Missing: a 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured channel (p. 16 lists ray tracing only as future work).
q2_support: p. 13: "When the number of vehicles varies, separate DNN models need to be trained", and the single model trained on K = 2 to 8 is tested on "the remaining 20% of data samples" of the same K values; p. 10: "4,000 of them are used for training and the remaining 1,000 samples are used for testing". Missing: a test on a scenario, array, speed or channel not in training.
q3_support: p. 11: non-learned "MMSE beamforming with perfect CSI" and "EKF [12]"; learned "we extend the HCL-Net approach proposed in [15]", "FC: This network uses three FC layers" and "CNN: This DNN structure includes a 2-layer CNN", compared on achievable sum-rate (Fig. 8): "always outperform the EKF algorithm".
q4_support: p. 8: "computational complexity for online beamforming" Con in Eq. (27) with the offline cost in Eq. (26); p. 16, Table I "ONLINE EXECUTION RUNTIME COMPARISON": 1.18 ms for OSPB versus 25 ms for EKF at N = 64.
q5_support: p. 10: "we generated 5,000 samples" from the own simulator, with no code or data link or DOI anywhere in the paper. Missing: any release of code or data, or use of a public channel dataset.
notes: Included as area 5 (ISAC): the DNNs predict transmit and receive beamformers from sensing echoes. q3 is 1 because E-HCL extends the earlier learned HCL-Net [15] (with perfect CSI, p. 11) and FC and CNN are standard networks on the same problem. q2 for the reviewer: Sec. V-C (p. 13) trains one model over K = 2 to 8 and tests on a held-out 20% of those same K, which I counted as a hold-out of the same data; the multipath test trains with the multipath channel as label (p. 15), so it is not an unseen condition. Table I was read as a page image (p. 16).
